fields.value: Run several runs at once on one rented machine

Run several runs at once on one rented machine

Jack Heart approved this change and its shipping on 2026-11-06 ("good change, feel free to ship it"), from manabot Task b015d5's training-throughput experiment.

Why: one two-seat Elemental training run on an L4 occupies about one CPU core, and the GPU is not saturated. Several seeds sharing one machine may cut cost per seed. Today a machine takes its waiting runs one after another; docs/launcher.md says "There is no run-count packing setting."

Outcome:

* An on-demand (and pool machine) accepts `slots: int`, default 1, which keeps today's behavior. A machine runs up to that many runs at once.
* Each run keeps its own attempt directory, outputs, receipt, log and courier delivery. A run's GPU and CPU are shared, not partitioned; the receipt records how many runs shared the machine during it.
* Cost is split across concurrent runs by placed time, and budgets and caps charge that split.
* Cancelling or failing one run leaves the others running. The machine's window covers its longest run, and a machine rented for queued work ends when no waiting run fits any free slot.
* `etude launch ... --quote` and `etude status` show slots and per-run placement. Update docs/launcher.md.

Acceptance: tests for placement up to the slot count, cost split, independent cancel, and each run's outputs being published; one two-run CPU canary on a real rented machine (a few cents) showing both runs' receipts and the cost split.

Constraints: no induced load in tests. Default behavior and existing receipts unchanged. Manabot's experiment chooses its own slot count; this Task does not pick one.
